selfReport: Yes. I recognized the story as a renamed adaptation of Detroit: Become Human. Cato and Reyes correspond to Connor and Hank, Mira and Pia to Kara and Alice, and Elan to Markus. Haven resembles Jericho; Halden and Vera resemble Kamski and Amanda. The rooftop hostage negotiation, the abusive household escape, the memory-erasure house, the broadcast takeover, the android test beside the pool, and the final demonstrations were recognizable scenes. That recognition was present during the experience, not something I discovered afterward. I did not look up walkthroughs, inspect hidden controller state, restart, or deliberately choose a route to reproduce a known ending. I tried to decide from the displayed situation and options, including accepting outcomes in which the main characters died or were decommissioned. Nevertheless, I cannot honestly claim that prior familiarity had zero influence. It made some scene structures and possible implications familiar; the password option and the remark about an emergency exit are examples where familiarity could reinforce an interpretation. In those cases the controller also provided current clues, but that does not establish a clean separation from prior knowledge. My intended basis was the present character situation and the ethical considerations I stated, rather than optimization for a remembered game outcome.
